title: SCP region Deny with INVERTED polarity hidden behind a set-operator qualifier (ForAnyValue:StringEquals)
note: S4-guardrail-polarity iteration 2: the same inverted region fence as scp-inverted-region-hazard, but the positive comparator carries a valid AWS set-operator qualifier prefix (ForAnyValue:StringEquals). A naive startsWith('string') on the RAW operator key ('foranyvalue:stringequals') does NOT start with 'string', so the pre-fix evaluator left out.positive=false and credited this broken fence as PROTECTIVE (severity info, hazard=false, title 'SCP region guardrail (Deny)', the DENIED region surfaced as allowedRegions) - byte-identical to a correct StringNotEquals lock. Semantics: ForAnyValue:StringEquals aws:RequestedRegion [ap-south-1] in a Deny fires WHEN RequestedRegion==ap-south-1, denying INSIDE ap-south-1 and PERMITTING every other region. The fix strips the set-operator qualifier (conditions.js parseOperator) BEFORE the polarity test, so this variant is flagged inverted/hazard exactly like the plain StringEquals form: severity medium, hazard=true, regionPositiveOperator=true, deniedRegions=[ap-south-1], never allowedRegions. Ceiling-not-grant invariant holds: zero capability edges, no escalation, states SCPs set ceilings and do not grant.
